loadout.attribute: Full Strength - three-way agreement between Amya's chaindart OP, the General Hero Guide's cross-class table ("Chaindart: Full Strength"), and the wiki's own Tips. House note: the weapon can't reach 2k penetration on full Strength - putting some Agility in can reach the soft cap of pene if your weapon rolls aren't great, at the cost of Leadership. - Amya, house: Kazepos
loadout.genderNote: No Change (Amya) - no animation-variant note for this class, unlike Shortsword's dash-distance difference. Confirmed absence, not a gap.

armorSets.name: Rogue's Armour
armorSets.purpose: Best Armour before Epic schem, tied with Warbreaker - no stated preference. Standard light rare set: 2pc +250 all-type armour penetration, 4pc +96 crit value.

armorSets.name: Warbreaker
armorSets.purpose: Best Armour before Epic schem, tied with Rogue's - no stated preference. 3pc crit window after enhancement skills, 5pc self-Bleed proc on hit.

armorSets.name: Sand Scorpion Armour
armorSets.purpose: Epic Schematic - Not Needed But Nice to Have. Heavy cooldown reduction across the whole kit, the pick for playing chaindart longterm.

spells.fillerNotes: Not a choice - there is only 1 possible skill setup for chain dart & scimitar users, all 4 skills are always equipped. - wiki, Skill Selection

builds.name: Rogue's / Warbreaker
builds.summary: Default before you have the epic schematic - no stated preference between the two. Rogue's gives flat penetration (2pc) and crit value (4pc); Warbreaker gives a post-enhancement-skill crit window (3pc) and a self-Bleed proc (5pc).

builds.name: Sand Scorpion Armour
builds.summary: For those wishing to play chain dart & scimitar longterm - heavy cooldown reduction across the whole kit, turning the CD-refund loop into an even faster one. The build implied by the AA-tier Supply Kill TW/Rank special job: sustained pressure on a point rather than one cooldown-perfect burst.

builds.name: Partial Agility
builds.summary: Full Strength is the baseline every curated guide gives, but the weapon can struggle to reach 2k penetration on Strength alone. Moving some points to Agility can close the gap to the penetration soft cap if your weapon rolls aren't great - at the cost of Leadership.
builds.forWhom: Min-max adjustment, not a beginner starting point.

matchups.vs: Lone heroes who stray too far from their allies
matchups.why: excellent at killing lone heroes (wiki) - the dash/blink skills are built exactly for jumping onto a straying target.
Trap Prey dismounts them if they're mounted (Amya's note).
Scorpion's Snare's Winded effect can cancel anything, even CCi heroes.

matchups.vs: Exotics and other low-life, high-impact units
matchups.why: what you're deployed to protect on defense - or, read the other way, exactly what an enemy Chaindart player will be hunting on your side.
commits hard to one target - other heroes intervening in the fight face little threat from a Chaindart mid-combo on someone else. Retreat into allied troops/heroes to ward it off.

matchups.vs: Heavy/medium mobility classes after Sandstorm is down
matchups.why: Sandstorm is the only control-effect removal tool and has a fairly sizeable cooldown - step in too close right after disengaging and a heavy or medium class with some mobility of its own can push forward and kill you.

matchups.vs: Masses of enemy troops / units generally
matchups.why: nearly no applicability against enemy units, no large AoE - poses no threat to formation-CC-dependent units like Onna-musha or Men-at-Arms.

Amya's Orochi Samurai unit guide names Chaindart explicitly as its hero pairing ("any lock-ult class") - a Special Melee Infantry (Polearm) unit whose kit disarms targets and phases through enemy units for high minimum damage.
No explicit list of which units to bring alongside a Chaindart player was found from Amya or house sources. [GAP: explicit own-warband unit pairings for Chaindart players - vets/house question]

techniques.name: Animation canceling
steps: Training room: try roll-canceling, dismount-canceling and blocking on every skill to learn which are cancelable.
techniques.rhythm: Amya: EVERY CLASS CAN DO IT! - Blocking is the primary cancel; roll canceling interrupts full spells, dismounts, and creates movement otherwise impossible. Costs extra stamina.

techniques.name: Active blocking
steps: it can be BROKEN and stagger you
techniques.rhythm: Don't get "Block checked" - Being an active blocker prevents undesired skills landing on you.

techniques.name: Horse-whistle CC immunity
steps: Time the whistle on the enemy CC
you take damage but no CC
techniques.rhythm: bugs out with PIN/LOCK skills, so care

techniques.name: Walk into braced units
steps: Walk (don't sprint) into their minimal range
techniques.rhythm: brace damage scales with your speed towards them - Largely moot for this class - Chaindart has nearly no applicability against enemy units and isn't built to fight into braced lines.

techniques.name: CD-refund cycling
steps: Leap and Slash for the Stinging Strike CDR
Scorpion's Snare's dual trigger off Leap and Slash/Sandstorm/Trap Prey casts
Stinging Strike between skills to shave more
techniques.rhythm: the kit is built to loop, not to be held for one perfect opener - Every skill in the kit shaves time off another - Leap and Slash's Stinging Strike trigger (-1s), Scorpion's Snare's dual trigger (-2s per Leap and Slash/Sandstorm/Trap Prey cast, -1s per Stinging Strike hit), plus the flat base-CD purchases (Butchery -2s on Scorpion's Snare, Fatal Sting -3s on Trap Prey).

gameplay.text: Chain dart & scimitar users have excellent mobility and can easily jump on and kill enemy heroes, but in turn have nearly no applicability against enemy units and are vulnerable to intervention by multiple enemies.
You are great to protect important units such as exotics (low life, high impact units), you are great to defend supply on TW.

roleLabel: The chain dart & scimitar places an intense focus on hero dueling.

positioning.intro: Where to be during a fight:

bullets.lead: Utility deployment, not a frontline or blob pick:
bullets.text: great to protect important units such as exotics (low life, high impact units) and to defend supply on TW.
Serve an area denial role - protect vulnerable allied ranged troops from enemy heroes diving past the frontline to strike at them.
Camp on or near a contested supply point in TW, ready to burst down whichever enemy hero is trying to pull it.
stand near your own high-value, low-HP units (exotics), ready to Trap Prey or Scorpion's Snare any enemy hero that dives past your line to reach them.
even CCi (crowd-control-immune) heroes - a standout utility callout.
that's Amya's own note, the wiki's own Trap Prey tooltip text doesn't spell out a dismount clause.

bullets.lead: The whole kit is unblockable and undodgeable -
bullets.text: and hits faster than most other weapons' abilities - but you're wide open while casting. Get caught with Sandstorm on cooldown, or hit by Winded/Thrown effects, and you can be beaten down fast.
jump on enemy heroes who stray too far from their allies - your dash/blink skills are built for exactly that.
this class isn't really played in sieges or ranked, it's used temporarily then swapped back to another class (LB or DB for example), or specially for TW.
Basically zero unit-fighting AoE, so it's a poor pick whenever the fight turns into units-vs-units instead of hero-vs-hero - the flip side of the AA-tier supply-kill specialty.

all four toggles off, the only class in this series where that's true. Amya's OP doesn't say why, but it tracks with free-aiming your dive kit onto one specific, likely-moving hero rather than relying on lock-on.
